messages.subject: plotting w/colsplit
parts:
hi all

i have a dataframe like this:

df<-
data.frame(p=rep(c(0,1),c(3,3)),t=rep(1:3,2),ga_0=rnorm(6),ga_1=rnorm(6),ga_2=rnorm(6),im=rnorm(6))
> df
p t ga_0 ga_1 ga_2 im
1 0 1 1.5162069 -2.2496957 0.6360539 -0.5963482
2 0 2 -1.0391362 1.2183491 -0.3332618 -0.5167709
3 0 3 0.5155268 -1.0733115 -0.1144858 -3.1545160
4 1 1 -0.8784321 0.7802412 -0.4710656 1.5022083
5 1 2 -1.2078294 -0.2180151 1.7768373 -0.1399839
6 1 3 -0.2146058 1.0239781 0.3688419 0.5582251


the numbers following the ga_ labels are times, so ga_0 is
ga at time 0, ga_1 is ga at time 1, and ga_2 is ga at time
2.

i want to plot something like

ggplot(aes(x=time, y=ga, color=im))+geom_lines()

for example, where time comes from something like colsplit
on the ga labels. im sure some combination of melting and
casting will do it, but i can't get it to work out. here's
my unsuccessful attempt so far

dfm<-melt(df,id=c("t","p"))
dfms<-data.frame(df,colsplit(dfm$variable,"_",c("v","time")))
dfms$time[grep("^[0-9]+$",dfms$time,invert=TRUE)]<-NA
cast(dfms,p+t+time~v)

t p time ga im
1 1 0 0 1.5162069 NA
2 1 0 1 -2.2496957 NA
3 1 0 2 0.6360539 NA
4 1 0 <NA> NA -0.5963482
5 1 1 0 -0.8784321 NA
6 1 1 1 0.7802412 NA
7 1 1 2 -0.4710656 NA

which doesn't plot the way i need it to.

any help would be greatly appreciated, and thanks for all
the help in the past!

best
-neal

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: plotting w/colsplit
parts:
Hi Neal,
You can rearrange the data like this

dfm <- melt(df, measure=grep("ga", names(df)))
dfm <- cbind(dfm, colsplit(dfm$variable, split="_", names=c("ignore", "time")))
names(dfm)[grep("value", names(dfm))] <- "ga"

but you lost me on the plotting part.

ggplot(aes(x=time, y=ga, color=im))+geom_lines()

is not going to give you a meaningful graphic, so now I'm left
guessing as to what the problem is. Did I misunderstand what you
wanted (if so how?)

Maybe you want

ggplot(dfm, aes(x=time, y=ga, color=im, group=im))+geom_point() +
geom_line(stat="summary", fun.y="mean")

but that seems unlikely given that im is continuous. Maybe you want

ggplot(dfm, aes(x=time, y=ga, color=im))+geom_point() +
geom_line(stat="summary", fun.y="mean")

or ???

Best,
Ista
